title: On the Wings of Tawakkul: Everyone Has Their Own Flight
titleUz: Tavakkul qanotida: har kimning o'z parvozi bor
body: Thoughts born at the airport, before takeoff: on walking your own path with trust in Allah instead of following in someone's shadow — written with love, and a little heartache.
bodyUz: Aeroportda, parvoz oldidan tug'ilgan o'ylar: birovga ergashib emas, Allohga tavakkul qilib, o'z yo'lidan yurish haqida — muhabbat bilan, ozgina kuyunchaklik bilan.

blocks.text:
Peace be upon you, my dear ones!

Another day of my journey. A passport and a boarding pass in my hand, clouds outside the window — it is in moments like these that the words you carry inside finally line themselves up on paper. Today I want to share, gently and with love, a thought I have been holding for a long time.

I have seen it many times: a person goes abroad to study or to work, and then brings along a relative or an acquaintance — someone with no language, no craft, no thirst for knowledge, just a fondness for seeing new places. When that person lacks responsibility — comes late, oversleeps, invents an illness — the burden falls on the poor soul who brought him: scolded by managers for mistakes that were never his own.

I have never brought anyone in tow, and I have never followed anyone anywhere. Every single time I set out with my mother's prayer and with tawakkul — trust in Allah. Türkiye, the Emirates, Russia, even Europe — I went trusting people I had never met in my life, but leaning, above all, on the One who created me.

This thought stayed unwritten until a Kazakh brother's wry question stirred it today: "Why does everyone among you arrive with someone in tow? Where is one's own opinion, own path, own effort? They even enter a shop in pairs; a man past twenty cannot stay alone in a room..." Bitter words — yet there is truth in them: everyone must have their own standards and their own road.

There come seasons in life when you must place your trust in Allah — sometimes with money, sometimes with circumstance. Say there is a person before you who seems God-fearing; you have asked around as much as you could, and he appears to be someone who shuns the forbidden. Now, for the sake of your goal, you may need to stake $2,000–2,500 — perhaps everything you have, topped up with the wages yet to come — on a business, on knowledge, or on reaching the country that can raise your craft to its highest form. That step is taken not with a trembling hand, but with tawakkul.

And by trusting Allah with circumstance I mean this: do not set out with the fear of "Will there be an Uzbek near me? Who will meet me at the airport? What if I get lost?" — set out entrusting yourself to Allah. If there are no Uzbeks beside you, believe me, it can even be better: otherwise, the moment you struggle, you ask in your mother tongue, receive a ready answer — and the lesson turns to ash. Alone, the obligation to learn a new language begins, a new way of thinking, a new approach, and relentless growth.

I am not saying "do not help" — helping is both a duty and a blessing. I only wish to offer a small, loving criticism of the excessive fear and over-caution in our youth today. After all, each of us carries different dreams, different roads, different chances. To be honest, I myself do not yet have the knowledge, the ability, or the means to help those who have asked me — which is exactly why I believe we must all understand one another. If anyone who once sought my help finds these words heavy, may they not weigh on you: my love for you is boundless, and may Allah be pleased with you all. These words are addressed to all my Muslim Uzbek brothers — for this is the reality in every corner of our homeland.

Good night to you all! I entrust you to Allah. You are in my prayers — remember me in yours.
blocks.textUz:
Assalomu alaykum, qadrdonlarim!

Bugun sayohatimning yana bir kuni. Qo'limda pasport, bording-pass, derazamning ortida esa bulutlar — ana shunday damlarda ko'ngildagi gaplar o'z-o'zidan qog'ozga tizilar ekan. Anchadan beri ichimda olib yurgan bir fikrni bugun sizlar bilan, muloyimlik va muhabbat bilan, o'rtoqlashmoqchiman.

Ko'p kuzatganman: bir inson o'qish yoki ish bilan xorijga chiqadi. Keyin esa ortidan qarindoshini, tanishini, yaqinini yetaklab keladi. U esa na til biladi, na hunar, na ilm umidida yo'lga chiqqan — shunchaki yangi joylarni ko'rib yurishning ishqibozi. Mas'uliyat bo'lmasa, ishga kechiksa, uxlab qolsa, o'zidan «kasal» yasab olsa — jabrini yana o'sha yetaklab kelgan bechora tortadi: o'zi qilmagan ishlar uchun ham menejerdan dakki eshitadi, boshini egib yuradi.

Men hech qachon hech kimni yetaklab kelmaganman, birovga ergashib ham hech qayerga bormaganman. Har safar onamning duosini olib, Allohga tavakkul qilib yo'lga chiqqanman. Turkiyaga ham, Amirliklarga ham, Rossiyaga ham, hatto Yevropaga kelganimda ham — hayotimda ko'rmagan insonlarga ishonib, lekin avvalo Yaratganga suyanib chiqqanman.

Bu fikr yozilmay yurardi. Bugun esa bir qozoq akamizning kinoyali savoli uni qo'zg'atib yubordi: «Nega sizlarda hamma ortidan odam yetaklab keladi? Nega o'z fikri, o'z yo'li, o'z harakati yo'q? Do'konga kirsa ham birov bilan kiradi, yigirmadan oshgan yigit xonada yolg'iz qololmaydi...» Achchiq gap. Lekin o'ylab qarasam, unda haqiqat bor: har kimning o'z mezoni, o'z hayot yo'li bo'lishi kerak.

Hayotda shunday pallalar keladiki, gohida pulga, gohida vaziyatga — Allohga tavakkul qilishga to'g'ri keladi. Masalan, oldingizda Allohdan qo'rqadigan ko'ringan, qo'lingizdan kelgancha surishtirib, harom-harishdan hazar qiladigan deb bilganingiz bir inson turibdi. Endi maqsadingiz yo'lida — balki bor-budingiz, balki yetmay turgan oyliklaringiz bilan qo'shib — 2000–2500 dollarni biznesga, ilmga yoki hunaringizni yuksak maqomga olib chiqadigan yurtga yetish uchun tikish kerak bo'ladi. Ana shunda titroq qo'l bilan emas, tavakkul bilan qadam tashlanadi.

Vaziyatga tavakkul deganda ham shuni aytmoqchiman: «Oldimda o'zbek bo'larmikan, aeroportda kim kutib oladi, adashib qolsam-chi?» degan qo'rquv bilan emas — Allohimga tavakkul qilib chiqish tavsiya etiladi. Yoningizda o'zbek bo'lmasa, ishoning, ba'zan bu yanada yaxshi: qiynalganingizda ona tilida savol berib, tayyor javob olasiz-u, saboq kulga aylanadi. Yolg'iz qolganingizda esa yangi til o'rganish majburiyati, yangicha o'ylash, yangicha yondashuv va tinimsiz o'sish boshlanadi.

Bu gaplarim bilan «yordam bermaslik kerak» demoqchi emasman — yordam berish, albatta, savob va zarurat. Men faqat bugungi yoshlarimizdagi haddan ortiq qo'rquv va o'ta ehtiyotkorlikni ozgina, mehr bilan tanqid qilmoqchiman, xolos. Zero, har kimda turli orzular, turli yo'llar, turli imkoniyatlar bor. Ochig'ini aytsam, hozirda mendan yordam so'ragan insonga yetarlicha yordam bera oladigan na ilmim, na qobiliyatim, na moliyam bor — shuning uchun ham barchamiz bir-birimizni tushunishimiz kerak deb bilaman. Kimdir mendan yordam kutgan bo'lsa, bu so'zlarim unga og'ir botmasin: sizlarga muhabbatim cheksiz, Allohim barchangizdan rozi bo'lsin. Bu gaplar barcha musulmon o'zbek birodarlarimga — yurtimizning har bir go'shasida ayni shu holat takrorlanayotgani uchun aytildi.

Hammaga xayrli tun! Allohimga omonat bo'ling. Duolarimdasiz — meni ham duolaringizda eslab qo'ying.
